story: Until 2026-12-29 (32 days), options price MARUTI to move about ±5.9%, roughly 12,976 to 14,595. In the past, the price ended inside the range priced this way 61% of the time.
Options are cheap compared with how much MARUTI has actually been moving: they price 25.0% a year while the last month realised 37.1%.
MARUTI has actually been moving about 2.33% a day this past month: very high for it against the past year.
MARUTI futures trade 28.0 points above the price itself. That premium works out to 2.3% a year, within its usual range for the past year.

iv.simple: Options on MARUTI are priced for moves of about 1.57% a day. That is normal for MARUTI compared with the past year.
iv.analyst: 30-day constant-maturity ATM IV 25.0%: 69th percentile of 1 year, 49th of all days since 2019-01-01.

vrp.simple: Options are cheap compared with how much MARUTI has actually been moving: they price 25.0% a year while the last month realised 37.1%.
vrp.analyst: IV30 - RV21 = -12.1 vol points, 1st percentile of the past year. Since 2019-01-01, IV30 was above the volatility that actually followed over the next 21 sessions on 67% of days: option sellers are usually paid a premium for carrying the risk, and the gap is what that premium looks like today.

term.simple: Near and far options on MARUTI are priced about the same: nothing special is expected soon.

skew.simple: Calls and puts the same distance from the price cost about the same (gap -0.3 vol points): no strong demand for either protection or upside. Puts usually cost more than this for MARUTI: against the past year the gap is on the high side, so less fear is priced than usual.
skew.analyst: 25-delta risk reversal -0.28 vol pts (front month), 77th percentile of the past year. More negative = more demand for downside insurance relative to upside.

realised.simple: MARUTI has actually been moving about 2.33% a day this past month: very high for it against the past year.
realised.analyst: RV21 37.1% (98th percentile of the past year), RV5 31.5%, RV63 30.0%; RV5/RV63 compression at the 57th percentile.

oi.simple: For the 2026-12-29 expiry, the biggest pile of call positions is at 14,500 (+5.3% away) and the biggest pile of put positions is at 13,000 (-5.6%). Option sellers defend these levels, so price often slows near them, but they shift as positions change.
oi.analyst: Front-expiry PCR (OI) 0.80; all-expiry OI PCR at the 83rd percentile of the past year. Today's change: calls +110,650, puts -44,450 (OI units, i.e. shares or index quantity). A high PCR in India mostly reflects put writing, so it is read as crowding, not as a signal.

futures.simple: MARUTI futures trade 28.0 points above the price itself. That premium works out to 2.3% a year, within its usual range for the past year.
futures.analyst: Near-month basis +28.0, annualised carry 2.3% (15th percentile of the past year; its 1-year median 6.0%). Last 5 sessions (price x OI, same contracts day to day): Long build-up, Long build-up, Long build-up, Long unwinding, Long unwinding. Build-up labels describe what happened to positions; they do not say who is right.

move.simple: Until 2026-12-29 (32 days), options price MARUTI to move about ±5.9%, roughly 12,976 to 14,595. In the past, the price ended inside the range priced this way 61% of the time.
move.analyst: ATM straddle / forward = 5.87% (forward 13,785.9). Scored on 1,954 days since 2019-01-01 against the official close on each expiry; a straddle is the market's mean absolute move, so about 57% inside is what a fair price would give.

notes.text: MARUTI has used 13% of its market-wide position limit (the ban starts at 95%).
